page: Google Cloud Platform z4m-highmem-192-cd is an enterprise-tier storage-optimized virtual machine powered by x86_64 processor architecture. The host configuration pairs 192 dedicated vCPUs with 1488 GB of system memory, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per core. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators and incorporates no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on internal routing or customer-allocated networking.

The primary differentiator of this instance is its direct-attached local storage capacity. Equipped with 180389 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across bundled physical solid-state drives, it is structured to support IO-intensive environments without relying entirely on external network block storage volumes.

From an operational cost perspective, this configuration aggregates compute, massive system memory, and ultra-high-density storage within a single boundary. This consolidation mitigates per-gigabyte network egress and attached disk latency costs. However, administrators must handle data durability at the architectural layer, as local NVMe drives are ephemeral and subject to data loss during host restarts or hardware failures.

Workload allocation aligns with enterprise applications that require both immense memory caches and rapid persistent disk operations. Common implementations include massive distributed NoSQL databases, in-memory transactional processing engines with local checkpoints, high-throughput log aggregation platforms, and large-scale data analytics clusters.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4m-highmem-192-cd is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive and memory-demanding workloads. Utilizing an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1488 GB of system memory, yielding 7.75 GB of RAM per core. A central feature of this server is its integration of 180389 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, which supplies high IOPS and ultra-low latency relative to network-attached disks. The instance includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not contain GPU hardware. By consolidating expansive compute threads, substantial physical RAM, and immense local solid-state storage into a single host, it provides high resource density for demanding backends. Suitable deployment environments include large-scale distributed databases, transactional processing, big data processing pipelines, and real-time analytical engines requiring rapid input-output operations.
